title: FatterJam
tagline: A living-room jukebox my wife and I run from our phones.
what: A jukebox for our living room. YouTube plays on the TV, my wife and I add songs and steer it from our phones, and the queue lives on a server, so nothing wipes it. A second mode plays my own music library at my desk.
built: Kept the queue on the server, so restarting or unplugging the TV can't wipe it
Made the TV screen and the phone remote update together, with pause and volume on the phone
Built a native Android TV app in Kotlin and installed it on our Chromecast
Added a desk-radio mode over my own 4,965 MP3s that never touches the house queue
credit: I wrote it; yt-dlp and ytmusicapi find the songs

making.problem: When we get home and want music, we open YouTube on the TV and scroll the same suggestions week after week, and one wrong tap can wipe the queue.
how: A small server finds each song and hands its video to the TV.
The queue lives in a database on the server. The TV and every phone listen to it, so a change on one shows on the others at once.
A native app on the Chromecast shows the video and what is next. The phone adds songs, pauses, changes the volume, skips and can undo a clear.
Desk mode plays my own collection in rotation: songs not yet played come first, and no album repeats within eight songs.
credits: Song search and streams: yt-dlp and ytmusicapi

moment.what: Desk mode went live on Oct 1 over 389 albums and 4,965 songs. It plays everything it hasn't played before it repeats anything, and a song I skip three times early gets benched.
